decisions.reason: The approved Hero V remains unchanged and serves only as the fixed source geometry for the revised second V.
The E and L provide height and integration references, but the source does not change their geometry or architectural language.
The source revises the Hero V–second V relationship without changing the established Hero V and É accent peak alignment.

Creating the second V as a proportional copy of the approved Hero V necessarily carries the Hero V's signature geometry into the second V, superseding the prior exclusion of the second V from this shared treatment.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Thank you for restoring the foundation. I think we're much closer now.

Before we continue refining the alphabet, I'd like to revisit one aspect of the VvÉ system. Looking back at our earlier explorations, I prefer the hierarchy between the Hero V and the second V in concepts #2 and #3 (attached). I don't think the current proof has quite achieved that same relationship yet.

Will you please show these two options?

Option 1: Create the second V by copying the approved Hero V and reducing it proportionally as a single object (without redrawing it). It should remain a true scaled version of the Hero V while still extending above the E and L.

Option 2: Start with that same copied-and-scaled Hero V, then make only the minimal optical refinements you feel are necessary so it integrates more naturally with the alphabet while preserving the same identity and maintaining its elevation above the E and L.

Next, will you please refine the optical spacing throughout the word? I like the visual rhythm of the L–V relationship in this proof and would use that as the benchmark for balancing the remaining letter pairs.

I've attached the earlier concepts as a reference for the Hero V/second V relationship I'm referring to.

Thank you!

value_updates.terminal_role: Expressive signature geometry shared by the approved Hero V, its proportionally reduced second V, and the É accent; the É accent remains the literal terminal section of the approved Hero V right arm.
value_updates.evaluation_rule: Evaluate two second V treatments derived from the copied-and-scaled Hero V: exact proportional scaling or only minimal optical refinements that preserve its identity; retain the literal Hero V–É accent relationship.
value_updates.terminal_status: The Hero V and É accent remain locked; the second V treatment is reopened only for the requested copied-and-scaled options.

decisions.reason: The impact is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY establishing proportional scaling, the two geometry options, and reopening the asset for refinement.
The source's spacing impact is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY using the L–V rhythm as the benchmark for other letter pairs.
The requested second V options do not alter the locked literal derivation of the É accent from the Hero V terminal.
The source requests visual options and spacing refinements but does not change the requirement to explain design rationale with review rounds.
The source concerns black-and-white glyph hierarchy and spacing and does not resume or modify the deferred champagne material treatment.
